syncGuide.description: Explains every status, progress line, sync and action on the Sync progress page.
syncGuide.footer: Press ? anywhere on this page to open the guide, Esc to close it.
syncGuide.intro1: is how far a sync got last time. The next run starts from there, so nothing is read twice and nothing is skipped.
syncGuide.intro2: Each row is one sync for one connection. Health tells you whether it keeps to its schedule. Progress tells you where it is.

a-fetch.name: Fetch again
a-fetch.text: Puts a catalogue pass or a re-check back at the start, so the next run reads everything again. Order feeds cannot be moved back: their position is kept in the platform’s own format.
a-fetch.todo: Starting a pass over is blocked while a run is in progress.

a-history.name: View run history
a-history.text: Opens the list of runs for this connection, with the error of every failed run.

a-keys.name: Show technical keys
a-keys.text: Shows the internal name of each bookmark under its label. Useful when talking to support or reading logs. The raw value is always in Technical details inside each row.

a-run.name: Run now
a-run.text: Queues this sync to run straight away instead of waiting for its schedule. It continues from the bookmark, so nothing is read twice.

h-failing.how: The latest run for this sync failed.
h-failing.name: Failing
h-failing.text: The last run ended with an error. The bookmark stays where it was, so nothing is skipped. It continues once the error is fixed.
h-failing.todo: Read the error in the details. An expired token is fixed by reconnecting the account on the connection page.

h-late.how: Not moved or run successfully for 2× to 6× its normal interval.
h-late.name: Late
h-late.text: The sync is behind its schedule but still within reach. Often a busy queue or a slow shop.
h-late.todo: Wait one more interval. If it stays late, open the run history.

h-misplaced.how: The bookmark name names one platform, the connection is another.
h-misplaced.name: Wrong connection
h-misplaced.text: This bookmark belongs to a different platform than the connection it sits on. A sync was run against the wrong connection, so its progress is not trustworthy.
h-misplaced.todo: Report it to whoever maintains your installation. Do not start it over on this connection.

h-ok.how: Moved, or ran successfully, within 2× its normal interval.
h-ok.name: On time
h-ok.text: The sync ran recently enough for its schedule. Nothing to do.

h-plain.name: OK
h-plain.text: A bookmark with no schedule of its own, such as the stock write order. It is never late.

h-pushes.name: Pushes changes
h-pushes.text: The connection sends every change to OpenLinker the moment it happens, so there is no bookmark to keep. An empty list here is normal.
h-pushes.todo: If changes stop arriving, check the webhook on the connection page.

h-stuck.how: Not moved or run successfully for more than 6× its normal interval.
h-stuck.name: Not moving
h-stuck.text: The sync has not run for a long time. Orders or stock from this source may be missing in OpenLinker.
h-stuck.todo: Open the run history to see why. Check the connection is enabled and its scheduled task is on. Then use Run now.

k-completion-stamp.name: Remembers when a pass finished
k-completion-stamp.text: Shown inside the catalogue row as “Last pass done”, not as a row of its own.

k-event-bookmark.name: Reads new events from a feed
k-event-bookmark.text: When the raw value is empty: nothing has been read yet. The next run starts from the beginning of the feed or from the connection start date.

k-rolling-offset.name: Re-checks known items, one page per run
k-rolling-offset.text: When the raw value is empty: not run yet, or it just wrapped around. The next run starts at the first item.

k-sweep-cycle.name: Goes through the whole catalogue over several runs
k-sweep-cycle.text: When the raw value is empty: the last pass finished. This is the normal resting state between passes.

k-write-order.name: Keeps older stock numbers from overwriting newer ones
k-write-order.text: When the raw value is empty: no stock written to this listing yet.

p-checked.name: Checked up to item N
p-checked.text: A re-check that walks through items OpenLinker already knows, one page per run, and starts again from the top when it reaches the end.

p-finished.name: Finished, waiting for next pass
p-finished.text: The last pass went through the whole catalogue. The bookmark is cleared on purpose and the raw value is empty. This is the normal resting state, not an error.

p-inprogress.name: In progress: N items done
p-inprogress.text: A long pass through the catalogue is part way through. Big catalogues take several runs, so one pass can span hours. It continues on the next run on its own.

p-notstarted.name: Not started yet
p-notstarted.text: This sync has never read anything. Normal for a new connection, or for a feature switched on recently. If it stays like this, look at its health badge.

p-readupto.name: Read up to (time)
p-readupto.text: Everything the platform reported before this moment is already in OpenLinker. The next run asks only for what came after.

p-stock.name: Stock sent to N listings
p-stock.text: One entry per listing, recording the newest stock number sent there. An older number arriving late is refused, so a slow job can never put old stock back on a listing.

q-alert.name: Will I be told when a sync stops?
q-alert.text: Not yet. Today the “needs a look” box on this page is the signal. Check it after an outage or when orders seem to be missing.

q-empty.name: Why is a value empty?
q-empty.text: For a catalogue pass, empty means the pass finished. That is the normal state between passes. For any other sync it means nothing has been read yet.

q-late-ok.name: Nothing moved, so why is it On time?
q-late-ok.text: A run that finds nothing new leaves the bookmark where it is. The sync still ran on schedule, so its last successful run counts.

q-nobookmarks.name: Why does a connection have no bookmarks?
q-nobookmarks.text: Connections that push changes to OpenLinker as they happen need no bookmark. Their list is empty by design.

q-safe.name: Is Fetch again safe?
q-safe.text: Yes. Starting a re-check over only reads. Starting a catalogue pass over re-reads every product, which adds load on the shop for a few runs, and writes nothing twice.

q-unknown.name: What is an unrecognised bookmark?
q-unknown.text: A bookmark this version of OpenLinker has no description for, usually from a plugin. It works normally; the page just cannot explain it.

s-catalogue.name: Product catalogue
s-catalogue.text: Reads every product from your master catalogue, a batch per run, so names, prices and variants stay current.

s-categories.name: Category tree
s-categories.text: Copies a marketplace or shop category tree into OpenLinker so pickers and search work without asking the platform. It runs in the background and has no fixed schedule to be late against.

s-changed-orders.name: Changed orders (backup check)
s-changed-orders.text: The shop normally sends orders by webhook. This check reads every order changed after the time shown, to catch anything a webhook missed.

s-deleted.name: Deleted products check
s-deleted.text: Looks for products deleted in your catalogue, so their listings stop selling.

s-listing-status.name: Listing status check
s-listing-status.text: Re-reads whether each listing is active, ended or blocked on the marketplace, one page per run.

s-offer-changes.name: Offer changes
s-offer-changes.text: Reads changes to your Allegro offers, such as an offer ended or edited on Allegro, so OpenLinker shows the same state.

s-orders.name: New orders
s-orders.text: Reads new and changed orders from the marketplace feed and creates them in OpenLinker.

s-parcel.name: Parcel tracking check
s-parcel.text: Re-reads the tracking status of parcels on the way, one page per run.

s-returns.name: New returns
s-returns.text: Reads returns buyers open on Allegro. Off by default, because the Allegro returns feed is still in beta.

s-returns-check.name: Open returns check
s-returns-check.text: Re-reads returns that are still open, one page per run, to pick up status changes.

s-shop-status.name: Shop order status check
s-shop-status.text: Re-reads the order status in the shop so a shipment marked there shows up in OpenLinker.

s-stock.name: Stock levels
s-stock.text: Reads stock for every product from your master catalogue, a batch per run. Changes go on to your marketplaces.

s-system.name: System checks
s-system.text: Checks that run across all connections, such as automation deadlines and stock shortfalls. They are listed under System.

syncProgress.description: Every sync remembers how far it got, so the next run continues from there. Check here that orders, stock and listings are still being fetched on time.
syncProgress.emptyMessage: Bookmarks appear after the first sync runs on a connection.

healthWhy.failingNoError: Last run failed. Open the run history for the error.
healthWhy.misplaced: This bookmark belongs to {keyPlatform} but sits on a {connPlatform} connection. A sync wrote it under the wrong connection.
healthWhy.stuck: Has not run since {when}. It normally runs every {every} min.

kindLine.event-bookmark: Reads new events from a feed.
kindLine.rolling-offset: Re-checks known items, one page per run.
kindLine.sweep-cycle: Goes through the whole catalogue over several runs.
kindLine.write-order: Keeps older stock numbers from overwriting newer ones.

syncProgress.pushesNote: {name} sends changes to OpenLinker as they happen, so it keeps no bookmarks. That is normal.

rewind.consequenceCheck: The next run re-checks from the first item. Nothing is written to the platform.
rewind.consequencePass: The current pass is dropped and the next run starts from item 1. Every product is read again, which adds load on the shop for several runs.
rewind.done: Done. The next run starts over.
rewind.passFinished: The last pass already finished. Use Run now to start the next one early.
rewind.restartCheckHint: The next run starts again from the first item.
rewind.restartPassHint: Drops the current pass. The next run reads the whole catalogue from item 1.

sheet.description: Details of one sync bookmark: where it is, its runs, and what you can do.
sheet.feedCannotRewind: Order feeds keep their position in the platform’s own format, so they cannot be moved back from here. Use Run now to fetch anything new.
sheet.runQueued: Sync queued. It runs in the next few seconds.
